title: Inference Fault Tagger and Latency Signal Consolidation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Our current error telemetry is fragmented across span logs, runtime metrics, and HTTP/gRPC status fields. Operations teams repeatedly struggle to attribute service-side latency to one of four actionable failure modes: client timeouts, upstream overload/backpressure, model-side rejections/errors, and transport-level codes (HTTP/gRPC). The lack of unified tags in traces and a consolidated dashboard makes incident TTR longer and obscures trends for capacity planning.

Goal: Implement a lightweight 'fault tagger' that enriches traces and metrics at tracehook ingestion time to produce canonical failure tags (timeout, overload, model_error, transport_http_<code>, transport_grpc_<code>, resource_pressure). Build a set of consolidated Grafana dashboards that surface a failure-funnel view and latency provenance timelines per route/model, and wire the tags into SLI rollups and existing alerting.

Scope:
- Instrument tracehook and span-enrichment pipeline to run deterministic tagging heuristics and ML-assisted fallback when signals conflict.
- Emit fault tags as string attributes on spans and as a discrete metric counter for high-cardinality slicing.
- Create a "Failure Lens" dashboard that aggregates by tag, route, model_version, region, and pod_pool.
- Wire tags into the SLI pipeline so that error budgets and regression alerts can be filtered by failure class.
- Sampling & storage: keep full-rich spans for 100% of failed requests for 7d; sample successful traces at 1% for baseline.

Out of scope: auto-remediation and traffic routing changes. This ticket focuses on observability and tooling for diagnosis and trend analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Tracehook enrichment emits a single canonical 'fault_tag' attribute on terminal spans for >=95% of failed/finale requests within 2s of ingestion.
A discrete Prometheus-style counter metric 'inference_fault_tag{tag="...",route="...",model="..."}' is available for dashboarding and SLI calculation.
New Failure Lens Grafana dashboard exists with: top-level funnel by failure class, latency provenance timeline, and per-route-tag slices; dashboard reviewed by oncall and PM.
SLI pipeline accepts fault_tag filter; two alerting rules added: 'unexpected degradation by failure_tag' and 'rising timeout rate > threshold' with documented runbook.
End-to-end tests: synthetic harness (local and staging) produces expected tags for injected scenarios (timeout, overload, model-error, 502/503/14 gRPC).
technical_notes: Tagging rules (priority order): explicit span error_reason field from runtime -> http/grpc status codes -> model rejection code (model API) -> backpressure indicators (queue_depth, queue_time > 50ms, cpu_nv_util > 85%) -> timeout heuristics (client deadline < server finish or kernel OOM).

Implement as a stateless enrichment step in the tracehook ingestion service; keep logic compact to avoid added tail-latency. Use a feature-flag to turn on ML-assisted disambiguation which consults a small decision tree model when signals disagree.

Metric export: emit Prometheus remote-write counters from enrichment step; for high-cardinality slices (model_version/route) use a cardinality cap and hashed bucketing for cost control, plus a label 'sampled_full=true' when full span captured.
Storage & retention: failed_trace retention 7d full, successful sampled traces 1% for 30d aggregated metrics; coordinate with infra to reserve additional ES storage for 2 weeks during rollout.

Privacy/security: fault_tag never contains PII; any span attribute used in tagging must be sanitized. Security review not required for algorithmic change but confirm with compliance if we add new sampled payload retention policies.
rollout_plan: Week 1 (staging): deploy enrichment binary behind feature-flag; run in 'dry-run' mode where tags are added to spans and exported to an internal topic but not used by alerts.
Week 2 (canary): enable tag counters in canary region for 5% of production traffic; validate tag distribution vs baseline and perform signal quality checks.
Week 3 (global): enable enrichment for all regions; enable Failure Lens dashboards read-only; invite SRE/PM/DS to review and signoff.
Week 4 (alerts): add tag-aware alerting rules and update runbooks; monitor for false-positives for 2 weeks then iterate on heuristics.

2025-02-18 — Design (Marco Silva): Suggested color palette for Failure Lens to maintain parity with existing SLO visuals; uploaded assets at https://drive.redwood/designs/failure-lens-v1.
